config.title: Build global event bus pub sub

intro.title: Build global event bus pub sub
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a global event bus, a design pattern that enables different parts of a JavaScript application to communicate without direct dependencies. You will learn the publish-subscribe (pub/sub) concept, where components can 'publish' events and 'subscribe' to listen for them. The implementation will involve core JavaScript constructs like objects, arrays, and functions to manage event listeners and data. By the end, you'll have a reusable event bus that demonstrates decoupled communication in a simple, beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: A global event bus enables decoupled communication between components in complex applications. In e-commerce sites, it synchronizes shopping cart updates across product cards, header counters, and checkout panels without direct dependencies. Dashboard applications use event buses to coordinate filter changes across multiple data visualizations and data tables. This pattern also powers notification systems where alerts from various modules need to broadcast to multiple UI areas simultaneously.

objectives: Construct a global event bus object to manage pub/sub communication
Implement a subscribe method to register event handlers
Apply a publish method to trigger events and execute handlers
Configure an unsubscribe method to remove specific event listeners
Initialize the event bus with a centralized events registry
Integrate the event bus to decouple components in a simple application
Manipulate event data payloads during publishing and subscription

steps.title: Create the EventBus class structure
steps.instruction: Create an EventBus class with a constructor that initializes an empty events object.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword to define EventBus, and in the constructor, set this.events to an empty object {}.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic EventBus class ready to store event listeners.
successCriteria: EventBus class is defined with a constructor that sets this.events to an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the class definition and a constructor that initializes this.events = {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a class named EventBus with a constructor that sets this.events to an empty object.

steps.title: Implement the subscribe method
steps.instruction: Inside the EventBus class, add a subscribe method that takes eventName and callback parameters and stores the callback in an object property.
steps.hint: Create a method named subscribe that adds the callback to an array for the given event name. You'll need to initialize a storage object first.
steps.expectedOutcome: The EventBus class will have a subscribe method that can register callbacks for specific event names.
successCriteria: EventBus class has a subscribe method that accepts eventName and callback parameters and stores callbacks in an organized structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your subscribe method properly stores the callback in a way that allows multiple callbacks per event name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscribe method isn't implemented correctly. Review how to add methods to a class and store data in object properties.

steps.title: Implement the publish method
steps.instruction: Add a publish method to the EventBus class that takes an event name and data,
steps.hint: Inside the EventBus class, define a publish method with parameters for eventName and data. Inside the method, get the callbacks array for that event name from your storage and call each callback with the data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The EventBus class will have a publish method that can trigger all callbacks subscribed to a specific event.
successCriteria: The EventBus class contains a publish method that accepts eventName and data parameters and executes all registered callbacks for that event.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a publish method, but it might not be calling all registered callbacks or passing the data correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The publish method is missing or doesn't properly trigger the subscribed callbacks.

steps.title: Implement the unsubscribe method
steps.instruction: Add an unsubscribe method to the EventBus class that takes an event name and a callback function,
steps.hint: Inside the EventBus class, define a method named unsubscribe with parameters for eventName and callback. Access the listeners array for that event and filter out the matching callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The EventBus class will have an unsubscribe method that can remove specific callbacks from event listeners.
successCriteria: The unsubscribe method is defined in the EventBus class, takes eventName and callback parameters, and filters the callback from the appropriate listeners array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an unsubscribe method, but check that it correctly removes the specific callback from the listeners array for the given event name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The unsubscribe method is missing or not properly implemented. Ensure it's a method in the EventBus class that filters out the provided callback from the event's listeners.

steps.title: Create a global event bus instance
steps.instruction: Create a global instance of the EventBus class and export it so it can be imported throughout the application.
steps.hint: Declare a constant variable named 'eventBus' and assign it a new instance of EventBus, then export it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A global event bus instance is created and exported, making it available for import and use anywhere in the application.
successCriteria: A constant named 'eventBus' is declared and assigned a new EventBus instance, and it is exported as the default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've both created the instance and exported it so other modules can use it.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a new EventBus instance and export it for global use.

steps.title: Create a subscriber component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Subscriber that subscribes to an event when mounted and updates its state when the event is published.
steps.hint: You'll need to use React hooks to manage state and side effects. Create a component that uses useState to store data and useEffect to subscribe to the event bus.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Subscriber component is created with state management and event subscription logic.
successCriteria: The Subscriber component is defined with useState and useEffect hooks, subscribes to an event in useEffect, and updates state when the event callback is triggered.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component includes both useState for managing state and useEffect for subscribing to events. The component should update its state when the event callback is triggered.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Subscriber component needs to be a functional component that uses React hooks. It should subscribe to events and update its state when those events are published. Review how to use useState and useEffect together.

steps.title: Initialize state in the subscriber component
steps.instruction: Inside your subscriber component, initialize state to store data received from published events. Use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'eventData' with an initial value of null.
steps.hint: Remember to import useState if you haven't already, then call useState(null) inside your component to create the state variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The subscriber component will have state initialized to store event data when published events are received.
successCriteria: The Subscriber component contains a useState hook call that creates an 'eventData' state variable initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with 'eventData' as the state variable name and initializing it to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscriber component needs state initialization. Use the useState hook to create an 'eventData' state variable with initial value null.

steps.title: Create event handler in subscriber component
steps.instruction: Inside the Subscriber component, define a function named handleEvent that takes a data parameter and updates the component's state with that data.
steps.hint: The handleEvent function should call setMessage with the received data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Subscriber component now has a handleEvent function that can update its state when called with data.
successCriteria: The Subscriber component contains a handleEvent function that takes a data parameter and calls setMessage with that data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it takes a data parameter and calls setMessage with that data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleEvent function should be defined inside the Subscriber component and update the state with received data.

steps.title: Wire subscription in subscriber component
steps.instruction: Inside the Subscriber component, call the global event bus's subscribe method to connect the handleEvent function to an event named 'dataUpdate'.
steps.hint: Use the event bus instance you created earlier. The subscribe method takes two arguments: the event name string and the callback function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: subscribing a handler to an event
bus.subscribe('userLogin', handleLogin);
steps.expectedOutcome: The Subscriber component will now be subscribed to the 'dataUpdate' event through the global event bus.
successCriteria: The Subscriber component contains a call to bus.subscribe('dataUpdate', handleEvent).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling subscribe on the event bus instance with the exact event name 'dataUpdate' and passing the handleEvent function as the callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscription isn't properly set up. Check that you're calling the subscribe method with the correct event name and callback function inside the Subscriber component.

steps.title: Create publisher component with event trigger
steps.instruction: Create a function named Publisher that returns a button element with an onClick handler that publishes a 'message' event to the global event bus with some data.
steps.hint: Define a function called Publisher that returns a button. In the onClick handler, call eventBus.publish('message', { data: 'Hello from Publisher!' }).
steps.expectedOutcome: A Publisher component that, when clicked, publishes an event to the global event bus.
successCriteria: Publisher function is defined, returns a button with onClick handler, and onClick calls eventBus.publish with 'message' event and data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Publisher function returns a button with an onClick handler that calls eventBus.publish.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Publisher component is not correctly implemented. It should return a button that publishes an event when clicked.
